fix_commit.message: avcodec/jpeg2000dec: fix integer overflow in dequantization_int_97()
fix_commit.author: Michael Niedermayer

findings.title: Signed integer overflow in dequantization_int_97() rounding addition
findings.message: In dequantization_int_97(), the sign-magnitude-to-two's-complement converted value `val` (an `int`) can be as large as `INT32_MAX` (e.g. via crafted/corrupted wavelet coefficients from the T1 decoding passes). Before shifting down by PRESCALE, the code adds a rounding bias `(1 << (PRESCALE - 1))` (with PRESCALE = 6, this is 32) using 32-bit `int` arithmetic: `val = (val + (1 << (PRESCALE - 1))) >> PRESCALE;`. When `val` is close to INT32_MAX (e.g. 2147483640), adding 32 overflows the range of a signed 32-bit int, which is undefined behavior in C and was flagged by UBSan/OSS-Fuzz ("signed integer overflow: 2147483640 + 32 cannot be represented in type 'int'"). This can lead to incorrect dequantized values, undefined behavior, or crashes depending on compiler optimizations.
findings.suggestion: Perform the rounding addition in a wider (64-bit) type to avoid signed overflow of the 32-bit int, e.g. use a `1LL << (PRESCALE - 1)` literal so the addition and subsequent shift are computed in 64-bit arithmetic before truncating/assigning back to `val`.

ground_truth.root_cause: The rounding-bias addition prior to the right shift in dequantization_int_97() was implemented using 32-bit `int` arithmetic without accounting for the fact that decoded coefficient magnitudes can be close to INT32_MAX, causing the addition of the rounding constant to overflow a signed 32-bit integer.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Signed integer overflow in dequantization_int_97() rounding addition
